quotes.quote: Editing a prediction changes its bytes; comparing its digest with an independently trusted expected digest detects that change. If an editor can also replace the expected digest, that reference no longer authenticates the original. Protected records, snapshots and receipts require actual storage and access controls, plus separate identities for revisions.

answers.reason: Separately protected evidence preserves the independent expected digest. An editable adjacent manifest or a recomputed digest cannot authenticate the original against that editor.

answers.reason: The tolerance fraction is 17/20 = 0.85, so it passes. Equal MAE is not strictly better, so the MAE gate and comparison fail.

answers.reason: Passing the local comparison gives comparison_pass true, while the synthetic-fixture restriction keeps decision hold and live_ready false.

quotes.quote: The seven weekday columns already span a constant, so this design adds no separate intercept. Fit weights by minimizing the sum of squared residuals.

For Friday February sixth, only the Friday indicator is one among the seven weekday entries. Elapsed time is sixty-seven divided by seven weeks; the known campaign flag is one. The actual fitted contributions are about one hundred thirty-one point three one two from Friday, eleven point zero seven one from trend, and twenty point nine from campaign. Their full-precision sum is one hundred sixty-three point two eight four. Clip a negative raw forecast to zero; this is still a point regression rather than a probabilistic count model.

quotes.quote: Dividing by the sum of the two costs gives pinball loss, with quantile level equal to underage cost divided by total cost.
Costs three and one give quantile level three quarters. The cumulative probability first reaches that level at one hundred sixty.

answers.reason: The quantile level is 4/(4 + 1) = 0.80. Cumulative probability is 0.60 at 80 and 0.90 at 140, so it first reaches 0.80 at capacity 140.
